title: One migration per redesigned game part, ranked by mods freed
text: Porting is one loop: python bench/exposure.py jars lists the mods of an update nearest to done, each with the references it still needs and what the game's own code did about each; the first one's reference gets a rule that names the game part, written from the game's own two versions; the same command shows the mod freed. The order matters more than anything else measured: on NeoForge 1.21.1 to 1.21.2 a mod held back has 15 references at the median and 1,241 of the 2,060 are used by one mod each, so the 100 references the most mods share free 2 mods, while 15 mods are one reference from done and 26 are done after 40 fixes (2026-11-20). The count then climbs steeply: 649 fixes for 80 mods. A removed method whose old body still compiles is inlined from it (163 of 1,234 for 1.21.2).
finish: 100 of the 150 most-downloaded NeoForge mods have nothing left for 1.21.1 to 1.21.2 (58 today); then the same for the next update
wrongIf: 25 references taken from the top of the nearest-to-done list free fewer than 10 mods
